title: Too young (Jeremiah 1:4–10)
hookLine: I'm only a child, says Jeremiah; before you were born I knew you

lines: FIRST DAY. A TASK TOO BIG.
cards: First day at a new job. Someone hands you a task three sizes too big, and the voice in your head is instant: I'm not ready. I'm too new.
Somebody older should do this. Now meet the next prophet. Jeremiah comes from a family of priests in Anathoth, a village in the land of Benjamin.
The book says God's word came to him in the thirteenth year of King Josiah. He'll spend the rest of his working life, through king after king, telling powerful people what they don't want to hear.
And his very first answer to God is that voice.

teach.h: BEFORE I FORMED THEE, I KNEW THEE.
teach.b: God speaks first, in the King James Bible: "Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations."

Knew, in Hebrew, can mean more than having information: the knowing of close relationship, even of choosing. Sanctified means set apart. Before he had a single skill, before he'd said a word, he was known.
And Jeremiah answers: "Ah, Lord GOD! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child."

teach.h: NA'AR: A BOY, A YOUNG MAN.
teach.b: The Hebrew word is na'ar: a boy, or a young man, a teenager or someone in his early twenties. The text never gives his age. It gives his answer: too young, not a speaker, not enough.

teach.h: GOD DOESN'T ARGUE: I AM WITH YOU.
teach.b: God doesn't argue. He doesn't say you're older than you think, or you're actually a gifted speaker.
He says: "Say not, I am a child: for thou shalt go to all that I shall send thee, and whatsoever I command thee thou shalt speak." And: be not afraid, for I am with you.
Then the Lord touches Jeremiah's mouth: "Behold, I have put my words in thy mouth." Like Isaiah's coal, the call goes to the lips, the very place he felt weakest.

teach.h: SAY NOT, I AM A CHILD.
teach.b: The answer to I'm not enough isn't you are enough. It's I will be with you.
Christians often read this call as a word to anyone who feels too small for what's in front of them, and some hear verse five as a sign that God knows each person before birth.

how: Jeremiah 1:4–10 is read at ordinations and services of commissioning, and is often given to young people in churches as a reminder that their age doesn't disqualify them from serving God.

o: a nickname for the boy Samuel in the Temple
an age limit the Temple set for its prophets
Jeremiah's first answer to God's call: I'm a child

games.q: what's inside the call — tap the pairs.

s: the Bible tells us Jeremiah's exact age at his call
na'ar can mean a boy or a young man. the text doesn't give his age.
God answers Jeremiah's fear with I am with you
not you are enough, but be not afraid, for I am with thee.
God argues that Jeremiah is a gifted speaker
God doesn't argue. he says say not, I am a child, and puts his words in Jeremiah's mouth.

games.q: you're Jeremiah. God says he set you apart before you were born as a prophet to the nations. what do you say?
o: Ah, Lord God! I cannot speak: for I am a child.
pick someone from the Temple instead.
games.why: Jeremiah says he's too young. God doesn't argue: he touches his mouth and says I have put my words in thy mouth.

practice: Name one thing you feel too small for, a conversation you've been avoiding, a job you don't think you're qualified for, and notice the excuse that comes with it: too young, too old, not good with words, not the type.
Then picture just its first small step, not the whole thing. If you pray, you can hold it before God with Jeremiah's honest words, I cannot speak, and then listen.

wordCard.voice: Too young. Jeremiah's first answer to God, I am a child, and God's reply: say not so; I am with you.

orig.note: Hebrew: a boy, a youth, a young man. it doesn't fix an age.

carryVoice: Your line: before you were born. Known before the first word. Day four hundred seventy-three.
